title: kate-ui: limit selection spans to the visible lines
summary: visible_selection_spans returns spans only for lines inside the visible range. A select-all on a long file stays inside that range. selection_spans stays as it is. Linux CI runs the test.

lane.reason: keys.rs has no GPUI type. Linux CI runs the test. It does not need a window or the owner's eyes.

definitions.definition:
#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
pub fn visible_selection_spans(buf: &kate_text::TextBuffer, selections: &kate_core::Selections, visible: std::ops::Range<u32>) -> Vec<SelSpan>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Add visible_selection_spans. Keep selection_spans and its tests. The visible range is half-open. A caret adds no span. A span stays on one line. The walk starts at the first visible line of the selection and stops at the end of the visible range. It does not build a span for a line outside that range. The newline byte stays on the line that ends there, as selection_spans does today. session.rs still calls selection_spans. Leave session.rs unchanged. The new function has cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code)). Leave paint.rs, layout.rs, and bar.rs unchanged. Leave session.rs, lib.rs, and files.rs in kate-ui unchanged. PKT-0051 owns those files. Leave bar.rs unchanged. PKT-0067 owns that file. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: keys::tests::visible_spans_cover_only_the_window
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because visible_selection_spans does not exist. The buffer is 4000 lines of x and a newline. The selection covers the whole buffer. The visible range is 10..12. The result is two spans, on lines 10 and 11, each with start_byte 0 and end_byte 2. A selection outside the range returns an empty vec. An empty range returns an empty vec.
